prompt: For a hereditary class $\mathcal C$ of finite simple graphs (closed under induced subgraphs), what relationship follows from the merge-width results, including the 4 November 2026 preprint?

answers.text: $\mathcal C$ is monadically dependent if and only if it has almost bounded merge-width.
answers.explanation: The November preprint proves dependence implies almost bounded merge-width. The reverse implication for hereditary classes was already known. “Almost bounded” means subpolynomial at every fixed radius.

answers.text: $\mathcal C$ is monadically dependent if and only if it has bounded clique-width.
answers.explanation: Square grids and their induced subgraphs are monadically dependent but have unbounded clique-width.

answers.text: $\mathcal C$ is monadically dependent if and only if it has bounded twin-width.
answers.explanation: The hereditary class of all subcubic graphs is dependent but has unbounded twin-width.

answers.text: $\mathcal C$ is monadically dependent if and only if it has bounded shrubdepth.
answers.explanation: All linear forests form a hereditary dependent class containing arbitrarily long paths, so shrubdepth is unbounded.

answers.text: $\mathcal C$ is monadically dependent if and only if it has bounded merge-width.
answers.explanation: Dependence permits unbounded merge-width: nowhere dense classes with unbounded expansion are examples.

answers.text: The implication from dependence to almost bounded merge-width remains conjectural at every radius.
answers.explanation: The cited November 2026 preprint states and proves it for every fixed radius.

answers.text: The November result proves the implication only at radius one.
answers.explanation: The earlier July 2026 result handled radius one; the November theorem handles every fixed radius.

answers.text: The result replaces “every positive exponent” with “one fixed positive exponent” in the width bound.
answers.explanation: Almost boundedness means every positive exponent, with constants allowed to depend on that exponent.

answers.text: The result gives one subpolynomial bound uniform over all radii simultaneously.
answers.explanation: The subpolynomial function may depend on the fixed radius. Uniform control of arbitrarily large radii is not asserted.

answers.text: The result says that every merge sequence of every graph in the class has subpolynomial width.
answers.explanation: It asserts existence of suitable sequences and gives an algorithm to find them. Bad sequences may still have large width.
